judgment.rationale: The report gives an exact sequence to verify on the open tray-menu PR, but does not confirm that focus actually moved to the taskbar.
evidence: The report describes a development build and links open, unmerged PR #51690.
The reported scenario starts in Notepad and uses Clipboard History from the tray entry point.
judgment.recommended_action: Compare the tray entry point with the keyboard entry point on the same candidate build.

issue_context.summary: Opening Clipboard History from the proposed Command Palette tray menu may lose the original paste target.
known_information: The reporter names Notepad as the initial foreground app and identifies the related tray-menu PR.
inferences: The clipboard action may activate the taskbar rather than restoring Notepad; the report marks this as suspected.
issue_context.analysis: Compare the previous foreground window and paste destination across both entry points. If only the tray path loses the target, use that result to guide the open PR rather than filing a separate implementation.
initial_investigation: Checked the issue timeline and verified that #51690 is open and unmerged. No runtime reproduction was performed.

fix_assessment.rationale: This is a pre-merge verification case for the open feature, not an established regression in shipped code. No separate PowerToys fix applies on the current evidence.

actions.label: Verify the tray menu preserves the paste target

prerequisites: Use a disposable Notepad document and a non-sensitive clipboard-history entry.
steps: Start with Notepad focused. Open the palette from the tray menu, select Clipboard History, and invoke paste on the test entry.
Record the destination and whether focus returns to Notepad or the taskbar.
Repeat starting with Notepad focused, but launch Command Palette using its keyboard shortcut as the control.
reproduce.expected_result: Both entry points paste the entry into Notepad. Neither should direct the paste to the taskbar.
